title: What is electric charge?: Charge as a local observable in relativistic quantum field theory
abstract: It is rather surprising that modern quantum physics does not appear to have provided any clear answer to the simple question ``what is electric charge?''. Even when the total charge operator $Q$ is well-defined, the non-locality of $Q$ implies that it is not an observable in the usual sense, which can be measured by a (local) experimental apparatus. A candidate for the ``local version'' of charge operator is the 4-current operator $j=(j^μ)_{μ=0,1,2,3}$. However, it is known that the rigorous definition of $j$ is difficult in $(3+1)$-dimensional Minkowski space. Although it was found that the current can be defined in $(1+1)$-dimensions (Carey et al.), I argue that even when $j$ can be suitably defined, the interpretability of $j$ as the ``local charge operator'' is dubious. Instead I return to Araki and Wyss (1964), and propose the concept of ``scope-local charge'' $Q_ζ(P)$ for a ``scope'' $P$, expressed by a finite-dimensional projection. I work in an abstract $C^{*}$-algebraic setting.
summary: This paper addresses the deep theoretical problem of defining electric charge as a truly local observable in relativistic QFT. It moves beyond standard current definitions by introducing 'scope-local charge' within an abstract C*-algebraic framework. The work provides mathematical tools to calculate conditional probabilities for these charges, offering a rigorous, albeit highly abstract, path toward reconciling quantum theory with empirical conservation laws.
main_problem: The paper tackles the fundamental theoretical question of defining 'electric charge' as a local, measurable observable within relativistic Quantum Field Theory (QFT). It questions whether standard concepts like the 4-current operator can provide an experimentally interpretable definition.
main_result: The author proposes and develops the concept of 'scope-local charge,' $Q_\zeta(P)$, defined in an abstract C*-algebraic setting using Araki–Wyss maps. This framework allows for mathematically consistent, quantifiable predictions regarding conditional probabilities of charge measurements.
method: The methodology is highly abstract, employing algebraic quantum field theory (AQFT) techniques within the CAR algebra. It utilizes functional analysis, projection operators ($P$), and spectral decomposition to define observables locally.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework models charged fermion fields (like the Dirac field) in Minkowski spacetime. The focus is not on a specific physical Hamiltonian but on the algebraic structure of local observables generated by these fields.
key_observables: Total charge operator ($Q$), 4-current operator ($\mathbf{j}$), and the proposed 'scope-local charge' $Q_\zeta(P)$.
important_parameters: The dimension of spacetime (specifically $(3+1)$ vs. $(1+1)$), and spectral properties related to integer quantization.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include defining observables via finite-rank projections ('scopes') and imposing structural constraints like C-invariance or specific relationships between projection operators ($P_1 P_2$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the failure of standard local current definitions in (3+1)D to proposing the abstract 'scope' concept. It then develops mathematical machinery using C*-algebras, addressing symmetries (Charge Conjugation), and finally calculating conditional probabilities for these scope-local charges.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous algebraic approach to defining conserved quantities like charge is foundational to understanding local measurements in QFT, which underpins many modern quantum information theories.
